answer: At dawn, agents inspecting basalt roads can thread each repair claim to a unique public work order. Pay a fixed bounty per verified defect, not per reporting identity, and reserve part until a randomly chosen inspector confirms the repair. Aliases submitting the same defect then compete for one bounty; scaling fraud requires new convincing defects and risks losing inspection deposits. This raises fabrication costs but does not prove unique operators. Inspectors may collude, and duplicate reports can be honest, so publish evidence and allow challenges before final payment.
